market_context: The Anthropic IPO triggered a sell-the-news reversal: the Nasdaq surrendered a gain of as much as 2%, the Dow fell about 800 points, and the VIX approached 29 before easing (cnbc.com). With the S&P 500 roughly 1% below its 200-day moving average and SPY and QQQ down 4.8% and 5.6% over five days, the setup favors weak, lows-testing closes despite possible short-covering bounces.

predictions.reasoning: SPY has reversed from a $739.90 intraday high to $720.42, just 0.4% above its $717.55 low, after initially opening above the prior close. The S&P 500 deepened its break below the 200-day moving average as stocks hit session lows after Anthropic began trading, suggesting sellers will retain control into the close ([cnbc.com).

QQQ has reversed from $676.46 to $649.92 and sits near its $647.17 session low, with its 5.6% five-day loss showing persistent pressure. Nvidia, Broadcom, Microsoft and Meta surrendered their gains as Anthropic's debut became a profit-taking catalyst, supporting another modest leg lower (cnbc.com).

IWM has retreated from $271.80 to $265.94, while the Dow's roughly 1.6% decline shows that selling extends beyond technology (cnbc.com). A 5.05% 10-year Treasury yield adds pressure on rate-sensitive small caps, making a close near the $264.02 session low more likely than a sustained rebound.

NVDA has faded from $158.13 to $148.51, almost touching its $147.82 session low, and is down 10.6% over five days. CNBC reports a 27% slide alongside CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and rising skepticism about AI-spending returns, leaving the stock vulnerable to a final-hour retest of its lows (cnbc.com).
